overloads.description: Decides if the objects are equal. Normally this command computes the result numerically. This behavior can be changed by using the Prove command.
Evaluates the expression according to the condition
Returns the quadratic function in the form: a(x−h)²+k. Example: CompleteSquare(x^2 - 4x + 7) yields (x - 2)² + 3.
Returns the quotient (integer part of the result) of the two numbers.
Returns the quotient of the two polynomials.
Calculates the greatest common divisor of the two numbers.
Yields all roots of the polynomial as intersection points of the function graph and the x-axis.
Yields one root of the function using the initial value a for a numerical iterative method.
Solves a given equation for the main variable and returns a list of all solutions.
Solves an equation for a given unknown variable and returns a list of all solutions.
Computes the binomial coefficient C(n, r). In CAS View, if n or r are symbolic, returns the binomial coefficient expression.
Factorizes the given expression over complex rational numbers (allows complex factors).
Factorizes the expression with respect to the given variable over complex rational numbers.
Factors the expression over complex irrationals.
Factors the expression with respect to the given variable over complex irrationals.
Solves an equation for its main variable and returns a list of all solutions, allowing complex solutions.
Solves the equation for the given unknown variable and returns a list of all (possibly complex) solutions.
Solves a system of equations for the given list of variables and returns all (possibly complex) solution tuples.
Solves a given equation for the main variable and returns a list of all solutions, allowing complex solutions.
Solves an equation for the specified variable and returns a list of all (possibly complex) solutions.
Solves a system of equations for the given list of variables and returns all (possibly complex) solution tuples.
Returns a list of all coefficients of the polynomial in its main variable (from highest to constant term). In CAS View the same syntax is available.
Returns a list of all coefficients of the polynomial with respect to the given variable.
Returns the list of coefficients {a, b, c, d, e, f} of the conic in standard form a x² + b y² + c x y + d x + e y + f = 0.
Returns a function whose equation is the lowest common denominator of the two given expressions.
Finds the complex roots of the given polynomial in x. Creates complex points in the Graphics View; in CAS View returns a list of roots. (Use CSolve for more general complex solving.)
Returns the (finite or truncated) continued fraction representation of the given number.
Gives the degree of the polynomial in its main variable.
Gives the degree of the polynomial with respect to the specified variable.
Returns the denominator of a rational number.
Returns a list {q, r} where q is the integer quotient and r is the remainder of the Euclidean division of the two numbers.
Returns a list {Q(x), R(x)} where Q is the quotient and R is the remainder of the polynomial division.
Returns the number of positive divisors of the given integer.
Returns the list of all positive divisors of the given integer.
Returns the sum of all positive divisors of the given integer.
Eliminates the given variables from the polynomial system and returns the resulting elimination ideal generators.
Expands and simplifies products and powers in the expression.
Returns a list {s, t, g} such that s a + t b = g and g = GCD(a, b) (Bézout's identity coefficients and the gcd).
Factors the given expression over rational numbers. For factoring over irrationals or complex numbers, see IFactor, CFactor, CIFactor.
Returns the list of prime factors of the given integer, each shown with multiplicity.
Interprets the given text as a number written in the specified base and converts it to a decimal integer.
Returns the geometric mean of the given list of numbers.
Returns the harmonic mean of the given list of numbers.
Factors the given expression over the irrationals.
Factors the expression with respect to the given variable over the irrationals.
Returns true if the polynomial is written as a factorization over the rationals (with positive leading coefficients), and false otherwise.
Returns true if the given number is an integer, and false otherwise.
Returns true if the number is prime, and false otherwise.
Calculates the least common multiple of the two numbers.
Calculates the least common multiple of all numbers in the list.
Calculates the least common multiple of the two polynomials.
Calculates the least common multiple of all polynomials in the list.
Returns the left-hand side of the simplified equation.
Returns a list containing the left-hand sides of each equation.
Returns the left-hand side of the equation at the specified index in the list.
Returns the larger of the two numbers.
Returns the maximum element of the list.
Calculates the arithmetic mean of the list elements.
Calculates the weighted mean of the numbers using the given frequencies.
Returns the midpoint of the segment joining the two points.
Returns the midpoint of the given segment.
Returns the midpoint of the given interval.
Returns the smaller of the two numbers.
Returns the minimum element of the list.
Writes a rational number as a mixed number (integer part and proper fraction).
Returns the remainder of the Euclidean division of the two numbers.
Computes (Base^Exponent) modulo Modulus efficiently.
Finds numerical solutions of the equation for its main variable and returns them as a list.
Finds numerical solutions of the equation for the specified variable.
Finds numerical solutions of a system of equations for the given list of variables.
Numerically solves the equation for its main variable and returns a list of solutions.
Numerically solves the equation for the specified variable.
Numerically solves a system of equations for the given list of variables.
Returns the smallest prime greater than the given number.
Normalizes the list of numbers, typically so that the sum of the elements equals 1.
Returns the numerator of a rational number written in lowest terms.
Tries to determine a numerical approximation of the given expression. The number of decimals depends on the global rounding option.
Determines a numerical approximation of the expression using the specified number of significant figures.
Parses the text as an expression and stores the result into a pre‑defined free number. Scripting command, assigns the value once.
Parses the text as an expression and creates a new number containing the result.
If possible, returns the partial fraction decomposition of the function in its main variable.
If possible, returns the partial fraction decomposition of the function with respect to the given variable.
Solves the equation in x, returns a list of all solutions and plots the corresponding points in the Graphics View.
Expands the expression of a polynomial function and simplifies the result, written as a polynomial in its main variable.
Creates the interpolation polynomial of degree n−1 through the given n points.
CAS: Expands the function and writes it as a polynomial in x, grouping coefficients.
CAS: Expands the function and writes it as a polynomial in the specified variable, grouping coefficients.
Returns the greatest prime strictly smaller than the given number.
Returns a list of prime numbers whose product equals the given integer (with multiplicity).
Calculates the product of all numbers in the list.
Calculates the product of the first n elements of the list.
Calculates the product of all list elements raised to their corresponding frequencies.
Computes the product of the expression for all integer values of the variable from start to end.
CAS: Calculates the product of all expressions in the list.
CAS: Symbolically computes the product of the expression over the given integer range.
Returns a random integer between min and max (inclusive).
If fixed is true, generates a random integer once (on file load / undo‑redo), otherwise updates on each recomputation.
Returns a list of the specified number of random integers between min and max (inclusive).
Returns a random polynomial in x of the given degree with integer coefficients between the given bounds (inclusive).
CAS: Returns a random polynomial in the given variable, with specified degree and integer coefficient range.
Creates a fraction equal to the given number and rationalizes the denominator if it contains square roots.
Returns the right‑hand side of the simplified equation.
Returns a list with the right‑hand sides of each equation in the list.
Returns the right‑hand side of the equation at the specified position in the list.
Simplifies the given expression or function, combining like terms when possible. May load the CAS.
Tries to tidy up text expressions, for example by removing repeated negatives. FormulaText is usually preferred for formatted output.
Solves the equation for its main variable and returns a list of all (real) solutions.
CAS: Solves the equation for the specified variable and returns a list of all solutions.
Solves a system of equations for the given list of unknowns and returns a list of all solution tuples.
Solves the given cubic polynomial and returns a list of all (possibly complex) solutions. CAS command.
Solves the given quartic polynomial and returns a list of all (possibly complex) solutions. CAS command.
Replaces all occurrences of ‘from’ by ‘to’ in the expression and evaluates numeric substitutions.
Replaces variables in the expression according to the substitution list (e.g. {x = a, y = 2, z = b}) and evaluates resulting numeric parts.
Calculates the sum of all elements in the list. Works for numbers, points, vectors, text and functions.
Calculates the sum of the first n elements in the list.
Returns the weighted sum of the list elements, using the given frequencies.
CAS: Computes the sum of the expression for all integer values of the variable from start to end (end may be infinity).
Converts an integer to its representation in the specified base (2–36) and returns it as text.
Returns all vertices of the conic section.
Returns the intersection points of the boundary lines of the inequality region.
Returns all vertices of the polygon.
Returns the n‑th vertex of the polygon.
Returns the start point (Index = 1) or end point (Index = 2) of the segment.
